Excellent! After **Bg7+ Kg8 Rxe5**, White has won the e5 pawn and the bishop on e7 is now hanging. Black cannot recapture on e5 (bishop is undefended). This is decisive.

**The key idea:** Bg7+ forces the king away, then the e5 pawn—which was just captured on—becomes undefended and can be captured cleanly with tempo (attacking e7).

**Coaching Note:**
When your opponent has loose pieces, play a forcing move *first* before you get distracted. Here, Bg7+ is check—it forces Black's king to h8, then attacks the undefended e5 pawn twice. By playing the check before capturing, you set up a fork: the rook attacks both the pawn and the bishop. Always look for in-between moves with check or threat.
